relations.subject: n1ql:like
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - hasExecutionConstraint. A prefix LIKE is turned into a range whose upper bound is the next string in collation order, so the rewrite is only correct relative to that order.

notable_absence.finding: Four absences. (1) No Related Links section, and only two outbound links in the whole page (sample buckets, query context). Every other page in this module ends with a Related Links list of four items, and all four of them - covering-indexes.md, index_pushdowns.md, groupby-aggregate-performance.md and early-filters-and-pagination.md - link INTO this page's #query-execution-details anchor. So the hub of the module is the one page with no way out of it: the cross-referencing is entirely one-directional, and a reader who follows 'Query Execution: Details' from any sibling page reaches a dead end. The same is true of the Capella copy. (2) The `exact` flag is never explained. It appears in the plan output of nearly every example as "exact": true, and is silently ABSENT in exactly the two cases where the predicate could not be fully pushed down (Example 18's leading-% LIKE and Example 29's unindexed function). early-filters-and-pagination.md makes exactness the decisive criterion for pushdown versus early filtering ('does not generate an exact index span, and needs to be evaluated as an early index filter'), so the field that decides the behaviour is demonstrated 30 times here and defined on a different page. (3) No version information except the stale note discussed in cross_component_finding: nothing dates span generation, the inclusion enum, EMPTY SPAN conversion, or the skip-key behaviour that index_pushdowns.md dates to 6.5. (4) No vector indexes: an 8.0 page enumerating what a predicate can become for every index kind it knows about (secondary, composite, array, functional, primary via meta().id) never mentions the three 8.0 vector index types or how a vector search request differs from a span-based scan. Also unexplained, though shown four times: spans built from query parameters ($1, $2). Examples 23-26 put placeholders in the low and high fields with no comment on what that means for a plan that is cached or prepared before the values are known.

cross_component_finding: This page has four internal defects, three of which are prose that contradicts its own tables and plan output. (a) Example 15 is titled 'EQUALITY Predicate on String Type' and its query is `WHERE name = "American Airlines"`, but the prose reads 'In this example, the predicate `name >= "American Airlines"` is pushed to index scan' - a range operator for an equality query. The span table on the same screen gives Low and High both "American Airlines" with inclusion 3 (BOTH), and the plan output agrees, so the prose is simply wrong. (b) Example 14's query is `WHERE NOT (id >= 10 AND id < 25)` but the prose says 'the predicate `id >= 10 AND id < 25` is transformed to `id <10 OR id >=25`' - dropping the NOT, so as written it asserts that a conjunction is equivalent to its own negation. The transformation shown is correct for the actual query. (c) Example 8's prose says 'This is a special case where the span is Low: 10, High: 5, and Inclusion: 0' while the table immediately above it says Low NULL, High NULL, Inclusion 0 and the plan says "high": "null", "low": "null". Both are true at different stages - 10/5 before the EMPTY SPAN conversion, null/null after - but the page never says so, so a reader comparing the three cannot tell which is the answer. (d) Example 20's span table labels its third row 'stops' where every sibling row is labelled with the predicate ('destinationairport = "JFK"'), losing the `= 0`. Separately, on naming: this page calls the components 'Query nodes', 'Query node', 'query engine', 'Query Service', 'Index Service', 'index service' (lower case), 'Indexer' and 'data node' - eight spellings of three services in one document, where the sibling early-filters-and-pagination.md is consistent throughout. And the stale version: an 8.0 page states 'In version 4.5, up to 8192 IN elements are pushed as separate ranges to the index service' in the present tense. Whether 8192 is still the limit in 8.0 is unknowable from the page; the sentence is dated in a way that cannot age.
cross_product_finding: Same three-way duplication as the rest of the batch - cloud/indexes/index-scans.md and server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/index-scans.md are both extracted already, and the module moved from learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/ to indexes/ between 7.2 and 8.0 - with two specifics worth phase 2's attention. First, the 'In version 4.5' note is present verbatim in all three copies (verified by grep in cloud/indexes/index-scans.md and server/7.2/.../index-scans.md), so a stale version reference has survived at least three releases and been carried across into the Capella product documentation unchanged. Second, this one page's central concept now has three ids in the corpus, one per copy: the server/7.2 round minted `n1ql:span` (plus `learn:index-scans` for the page), the Capella round minted `index:index-span`, and neither knew about the other. I reused `index:index-span` and did not mint a fourth, but a recurrence count that treats n1ql:span and index:index-span as different terms will read the single best-attested concept in this module as two weak ones - and will read `learn:index-scans` as a third. This is the clearest case in the batch for phase 2 resolving aliases before counting, rather than after.
